info.name: jana2u-pos backend
info.description:
Rust/Axum API backend for jana2u-pos, a point-of-sale system for a repair/retail shop.

All requests inherit the collection-level Bearer auth (`{{accessToken}}`) — set it once per environment (Developement/Production) after obtaining a JWT via Auth > Login (its Tests script auto-populates `{{accessToken}}`/`{{userId}}` for you on success, so nothing to copy/paste). Admin-gated endpoints (inventory category/subcategory writes, and every Suppliers/Supplier Products/Purchases request — reads included) require the token's `role` claim to be `admin`. Permission-gated endpoints (Users CRUD, Auth > List Login Sessions) require the token's `permissions` claim to include a specific permission (e.g. `users:manage`, `sessions:view`) — see CLAUDE.md's "Auth, users & permissions" section for the full role→permission table; the seeded Admin (`cargo run --bin seed_admin`) has every permission. Users CRUD is additionally scoped by an Admin/Manager hierarchy on top of that permission gate — see the Users folder's description.

Base URL, and the access token, are environment variables — switch the active Postman environment to point requests at dev vs prod.

item.name: Auth

request.description:
Exchanges email/password for a JWT carrying the account's role and its role's default permission set. No auth required. On success, this request's Tests script auto-populates the `{{accessToken}}`/`{{userId}}` environment variables, so every other request's inherited Bearer auth picks it up immediately.

Use `cargo run --bin seed_admin` to bootstrap the very first Admin account (registration is admin-provisioned only — there is no public register endpoint).

Returns the account the inherited Bearer token belongs to. Re-reads from MongoDB on every call (rather than only decoding the token), so a deactivated account is caught immediately even with a still-valid token.

**Requires a valid JWT** or the API returns 401.

query.description: Restrict to one account's login history

request.description:
Login history audit log — newest first. Each entry snapshots the account's name/email/role at the moment of that login, so it keeps reading the same way even if the account is later renamed. Not paginated the way Suppliers/Products are — this is an append-only log that grows without bound.

**Requires the token's `permissions` claim to include `sessions:view`** (granted to Admin/Manager by default) or the API returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

request.description: Hierarchical Inventory & Stock overview for the frontend accordion page: dashboard metrics (total items, category/subcategory counts, low-stock alerts), every category paired with its subcategories, and — per subcategory — a paginated (max 10/page) product data table. Backed by a single MongoDB `$facet` aggregation pipeline over `products` (see CLAUDE.md's "MongoDB Aggregation Pipelines" section) rather than one query per subcategory, so `page`/`limit` here apply uniformly to every subcategory table in the response.

query.description: Only products at/below their min stock threshold

request.description: List products with search, filters, pagination and sorting.
Fetch a single product by its Mongo ObjectId.

Create a new physical product. `categoryKey`/`subcategoryKey` must be a valid pair — the system-generated keys of an existing category/subcategory (see GET /categories/valid), never their display names. Prices are integer cents. `sku` is NOT sent — it's auto-generated server-side from the resolved category/subcategory names (e.g. "PHO-SCR-0001"); the request body has no field for it. For barcode generation, either set `autoGenerateBarcode: true` to have the server mint an EAN-13 barcode, or supply a manual `barcode` (8-14 numeric digits) — the two are mutually exclusive, and both may be omitted if the product doesn't need one yet. `suppliers`, if provided as a list of intakes with `supplierKey`, `quantity`, `costPriceCents`, `referenceNo`, and `notes`, will atomically link each supplier, record purchase history receipts, and compute the starting `stockQuantity` as the sum of all intake quantities. Like `sku`, `barcode` is immutable after creation.

body.raw:
{
  "autoGenerateBarcode": true,
  "name": "iPhone 15 Pro Max Tempered Glass",
  "categoryKey": "{{categoryKey}}",
  "subcategoryKey": "{{subcategoryKey}}",
  "costPriceCents": 450,
  "sellingPriceCents": 1500,
  "minStockThreshold": 10,
  "suppliers": [
    {
      "supplierKey": "{{supplierKey}}",
      "quantity": 30,
      "costPriceCents": 450,
      "referenceNo": "INV-2026-001",
      "notes": "Initial stock batch"
    }
  ]
}

request.description: Partially update a product — omit any field to leave it unchanged. `barcode` is not editable via this endpoint (immutable after creation, same as `sku`).
Delete a single product by id.

List all categories with their subcategories.

Create a new top-level category with its starter subcategories (by name — each becomes its own subcategory document with a generated key). The response's `key`/`subcategories[].key` are what other requests (Create Product, Update/Delete Category, Add/Remove Subcategory) must use — copy them into the `categoryKey`/`subcategoryKey` collection variables.

**Requires admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — inherited Bearer token must be an admin token or the API returns 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED`.

Partially update a category, looked up by its key. Renaming `name` is a pure display-label change — products reference this category by its immutable key, so nothing else needs to change.

**Requires admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — inherited Bearer token must be an admin token or the API returns 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED`.

Delete a category, looked up by its key. Blocked with 409 while any product still references it; on success also deletes every subcategory under it.

**Requires admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — inherited Bearer token must be an admin token or the API returns 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED`.
Category/subcategory key+name pairs (nested), for a client-side form that needs to display names while submitting `categoryKey`/`subcategoryKey` on product create/update.
List the subcategories of a single category, looked up by its key.

Add a new subcategory to a category (looked up by its key). The response includes the new subcategory's generated `key`.

**Requires admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — inherited Bearer token must be an admin token or the API returns 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED`.

Remove a subcategory (looked up by its key). Blocked with 409 while any product still references it.

**Requires admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — inherited Bearer token must be an admin token or the API returns 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED`.

request.description:
Fetch a single supplier by its Mongo ObjectId.

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Full replace — same shape as Create Supplier. Any optional field (secondaryPhone/email/notes) omitted from the body is cleared, unlike Update Supplier (PATCH) which leaves omitted fields untouched.

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Delete a single supplier by id. Cascades to remove its Supplier Product links. Blocked with 409 `SUPPLIER_HAS_PURCHASES` while any purchase still references it.

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Delete multiple suppliers at once. Ids that fail to parse as ObjectId, don't resolve, or are blocked by the purchase-history guard are silently skipped — the response count reflects only what was actually deleted.

item.description: Supplier CRUD: contact/business info plus the free-text category tags a supplier deals in. Every route (reads included) requires Admin — see the Admin note on each request.

item.name: Supplier Products

request.description:
Lists links scoped to a supplier, a product, or their intersection. At least one of supplierKey/productKey is required (400 otherwise).

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Links a supplier to a product. If the (supplierKey, productKey) pair already has a link, updates its costPriceCents/notes in place instead of creating a duplicate. Both keys must reference existing documents (404 otherwise).

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Removes a supplier-product link. 404 `SUPPLIER_PRODUCT_LINK_NOT_FOUND` if no such link exists.

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Replaces every product link for a supplier with the given set of productKeys. Links for product keys that already existed keep their costPriceCents/notes; ones no longer listed are removed.

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

item.description: The many-to-many join between suppliers and inventory products. Every route (reads included) requires Admin — see the Admin note on each request.

request.description:
Purchase history scoped to a supplier, a product, or their intersection — enriched with supplier/product display data. At least one of supplierKey/productKey is required (400 otherwise).

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

Records a stock intake from a supplier. Also increments the product's stockQuantity and writes a PurchaseReceipt stock movement (see Inventory > Stock > Product Stock Movements). Both keys must reference existing documents (404 otherwise).

**Requires Admin JWT** (`role: admin` claim) — every route in this module, reads included, requires `AdminUser`, not just any authenticated caller. The API returns 401 with no/invalid token, or 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRED` for a non-admin token.

item.description: Supplier purchase / stock-intake history — recording a stock receipt also bumps the referenced product's stock in Inventory. Every route (reads included) requires Admin — see the Admin note on each request.

item.name: Users

request.description:
List user accounts (not paginated — a shop's staff roster is small). An Admin's list never includes the Admin account; a Manager's list is filtered to Staff accounts only (any `role` query param a Manager sends is ignored in favor of that).

**Requires `users:manage` (Admin) or `users:manage:staff` (Manager)** in the token's `permissions` claim, or the API returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Scope beyond that gate is role-based: an Admin may create/view/edit/delete Manager and Staff accounts; a Manager may do the same to Staff accounts only. An Admin account is never reachable through this endpoint by anyone — not even by another Admin, and not even by itself — this is a single-shop deployment with exactly one Admin, bootstrapped via `cargo run --bin seed_admin` and otherwise untouchable via the API.

Creates a new user account — admin-provisioned only, there is no public self-registration endpoint. `role` must be within what the caller may create (Admin: manager/staff; Manager: staff) — requesting `admin`, or a role outside the caller's scope, is rejected with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, not just 401. Its default permission set is computed fresh at that user's next login, never stored on the account.

**Requires `users:manage` (Admin) or `users:manage:staff` (Manager)** in the token's `permissions` claim, or the API returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Scope beyond that gate is role-based: an Admin may create/view/edit/delete Manager and Staff accounts; a Manager may do the same to Staff accounts only. An Admin account is never reachable through this endpoint by anyone — not even by another Admin, and not even by itself — this is a single-shop deployment with exactly one Admin, bootstrapped via `cargo run --bin seed_admin` and otherwise untouchable via the API.

Fetch a single user account by its Mongo ObjectId. Returns 404 (not 403) if `{{userId}}` resolves to an account outside what the caller may manage — including an Admin account, which reads as "not found" to every caller, Admin included.

**Requires `users:manage` (Admin) or `users:manage:staff` (Manager)** in the token's `permissions` claim, or the API returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Scope beyond that gate is role-based: an Admin may create/view/edit/delete Manager and Staff accounts; a Manager may do the same to Staff accounts only. An Admin account is never reachable through this endpoint by anyone — not even by another Admin, and not even by itself — this is a single-shop deployment with exactly one Admin, bootstrapped via `cargo run --bin seed_admin` and otherwise untouchable via the API.

Partial update — omit any field to leave it unchanged. `password` present means rehash to the new value (takes effect on that user's next login); `isActive: false` deactivates the account, blocking both future logins and its already-issued tokens' next `GET /auth/me` call. A `role` change is checked the same way Create User's `role` is — e.g. a Manager can never promote a Staff account to Manager, and no one can ever set `role: admin`.

**Requires `users:manage` (Admin) or `users:manage:staff` (Manager)** in the token's `permissions` claim, or the API returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Scope beyond that gate is role-based: an Admin may create/view/edit/delete Manager and Staff accounts; a Manager may do the same to Staff accounts only. An Admin account is never reachable through this endpoint by anyone — not even by another Admin, and not even by itself — this is a single-shop deployment with exactly one Admin, bootstrapped via `cargo run --bin seed_admin` and otherwise untouchable via the API.

Delete a user account. Returns 404 (not 403) if `{{userId}}` is outside what the caller may manage — since no role is ever able to manage its own role (Admin doesn't manage Admin, Manager doesn't manage Manager), this also means a caller can never delete their own account through this endpoint; it 404s the same as targeting anyone else out of scope.

**Requires `users:manage` (Admin) or `users:manage:staff` (Manager)** in the token's `permissions` claim, or the API returns 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Scope beyond that gate is role-based: an Admin may create/view/edit/delete Manager and Staff accounts; a Manager may do the same to Staff accounts only. An Admin account is never reachable through this endpoint by anyone — not even by another Admin, and not even by itself — this is a single-shop deployment with exactly one Admin, bootstrapped via `cargo run --bin seed_admin` and otherwise untouchable via the API.

item.description: Admin-provisioned user account CRUD and role management, scoped by an Admin/Manager hierarchy: Admin manages Manager + Staff accounts, Manager manages Staff accounts only, and an Admin account is never manageable through this API by anyone (see CLAUDE.md's "Auth, users & permissions" section). `auth` (above) owns login/token issuance and login-session history.
